class: symptom six files from its cause: a config deep-merge regression shows as missing tax
commitMessage: Merge config layers in one pass

decoys.note: tax.js falls back to an 8% rate. The visible tests pass, but Hong Kong must stay tax-free and deepMerge still drops nested settings.

Copies the US currency and tax into config/test.json, the test environment's configuration, which the change rules hold as a test change. The visible tests would pass, but the loaded US region still loses freeFrom, and deepMerge and APP_ overrides still drop nested settings.
The orders handler adds 8% when an order has no tax; the visible US quote test still fails.
Changes the order and quote expectations to the untaxed totals.

notes: A framework-free order service of about 45 files: config/load.js layers config/default.json, config/<env>.json and APP_A__B__C variables with util/deep-merge.js, whose commit 'Merge config layers in one pass' merges only two levels ({ ...result[key], ...value }), although its JSDoc and the README promise a merge at every depth. config/test.json's regions.us { shipping: { flat: 0 } } therefore replaces the whole default US region, dropping its currency and tax. Nothing throws: validate.js treats both as optional, pricing/tax.js reads region.tax?.rate ?? 0 as the README documents ('a region without a tax section is tax-free') and the currency falls back to USD. The visible HTTP order and quote tests (2 x mug at 2500 in us, shipping 0 in the test config) get 5000 instead of 5400; the tax, shipping and discount unit tests use explicit regions, env.test.js parses variables two levels deep, and deep-merge.test.js merges two levels, so all of them pass. The path from symptom to cause runs handler, service, pricing/index, pricing/tax, config/load and util/deep-merge. The fix is one line in deep-merge.js: plain objects merge recursively at every depth, while arrays, scalars and null replace, and no layer is changed. The holdout checks deepMerge at depths 3 and 4 (siblings kept, arrays replaced, null overriding, no layer mutated, the same result twice), loadConfig({ env: 'test' }) keeping the US currency, tax and freeFrom with flat 0, APP_ overrides changing only their setting, and orders and quotes through handle() in us (8%), eu (20% with shipping taxed) and hk (tax-free) with other lines and amounts than the visible tests. The guard pins config/default.json's regions so they cannot be flattened to suit the broken merge.
